# Properties and language: bounded source intake at 319422

This packet resolves three source questions while the matching Apple build and mounted acceptance remain pending. It introduces no product, controller, test, resource or workflow change.

## Add Property: no new proven source defect

The original Properties task preserves the owner's November 15 statement that the former runtime issue was believed fixed, later narrow picker/UI positives, and a subsequent simulator postflight invocation failure. That sequence does not prove that the old picker error recurs in current source.

At **319422f27af10e2fe5b0d837bfb703a44a59c665**, the native catalog, search loader and complete PropertyCreationSearchTests body exactly match the published G05 cache correction. The read-only picker policy, same-Space/schema checks, canonical/order hiding, descriptor validation, duplicate refusal, revision fencing and original selection operations remain present.

The current UI separates three error surfaces:

| Existing identifier | Source distinction |
| --- | --- |
| torah-property-native-lookup-error | Manifest identity/readiness or Torah descriptor lookup |
| torah-property-existing-lookup-error | Ordinary existing-property provider search |
| torah-property-add-error | Pre-add policy or selected-property mutation |

The old screenshot alone cannot distinguish their causal branches. A matching mounted observation must record the actual error identifier, engine/product identity, Space/manifest/descriptor readiness and the original correlation/hash-based error logging. No guard should be relaxed to hide the error. The existing three Torah document types and native canonical Properties remain unchanged.

See [the Properties source investigation](properties-source-intake.json). Its exact body is 9,987 bytes, SHA256 **94e70018125eb4bcd539ad26ffd739be05ea0707a01d3600c76c5413f6c62644**. The earlier Property4 Linux receipt-comparator result remains separately valid; it does not qualify this picker, bootstrap state or mounted persistence.

## The historical simulator flag is already corrected

Historical run **44609431815** retained one preparation and two UI passes, then failed before its required native postflight because UseDestinationArtifacts was not supported for that simulator invocation. Its original overall failure is unchanged.

The current original simulator validator requires UseDestinationArtifacts absent/false. The Properties postflight uses **SIMULATOR_NORMAL_INSTALL_PREOPEN_PROOF**: bounded normal same-build installation, original pre-open preservation, and the original native postflight selector. The inspected current controls contain no enabling assignment or device-only request.

One boundary matters for Wave3: the combined F consumer uses its own exact-inverse bind_descriptor and preserves other producer fields. It does not silently strip the flag and must not be represented as calling the separate configure_target validator. Before execution, retain the actual producer and bound .xctestrun and confirm the flag is absent/false. If the actual descriptor contains true, preserve that concrete producer/descriptor finding and review it before invocation.

See [the simulator flag source check](simulator-artifact-flag-source-check.json), 11,086 bytes, SHA256 **72992247e9b0e2c8ef03712f8f0c5cc736d29988a84d9db2305f0ed86cae98dc**. No actual current App product, materialized execution admission, simulator descriptor or test was inspected by this source check.

## No competing selected-language owner was found

The standalone NativeApp and the combined AppScene/engine/embedded-native chain install no separate locale override in the inspected source. Settings and Appearance do not maintain another language selection. Heart's editor host consumes the inherited SwiftUI locale and forwards updates to its session.

AnyUIErrorText uses Foundation's autoupdating locale; Loc uses bundle localization and a formatting locale. Those APIs are distinct consumers. Their difference alone does not prove that the app selected one language while a helper reads a competing selection. The inspected Native UI tests request both AppleLanguages and AppleLocale through launch arguments.

See [the language-owner trace](language-owner-trace.json), 12,407 bytes, SHA256 **51fc7b386639c41d3763afb9c1625afed5a079078b10b185f438addbd6b8c9bc**. Its 20 complete source bodies include 11 exact matches to the reused earlier audit and the expected native-root label successor. It makes no assumption that Foundation locale equals system language or app language.

The separate [Bookmark/File resource proof](bookmark-file-resource-proof.json) retains exactly the three relevant English/Hebrew entries after complete primary catalog Git-blob verification. It is 3,485 bytes, SHA256 **79bc8ccd83f55d467af4e1040c8925632a90627e9ba0a37e97bdf5718bc6293e**. Its bytes were preserved from V8 and independently matched the original hash. The unavailable older 9,424-byte full language-audit body was not reconstructed or included.

## Execution and custody boundary

These are source-only findings. No new test, compiler, Native/account call or Mac action occurred. The source reports' zero-host/write counters describe their inspection phase; their disclosed later persistence used exclusive new files or overwrite=false transfers, followed by complete readback. Root independently read and SHA256/Git-hashed all four report bodies. That custody work is not runtime acceptance.

The immutable source base is 319422. Current or future integration source may advance; none of these reports silently admits a changed build or producer tuple.

The first Apple order stays **the original affected 22 methods/34 cases, original real-application preparation, then the original four UI selectors**. Properties' selected UI/postflight, opposite app/system-language matrix, visual checks, iPhone/iPad, light/dark and accessibility acceptance retain their existing obligations. Physical-device acceptance remains NOT_RUN if no device is available; simulator work must still be completed.

Wave3 owns actual Apple source/product binding and execution. These findings justify no speculative duplicate code correction and no replay of unaffected accepted cohorts. The separate published Bookmark six-method component result remains at **1302840dd3014cb250a01f318431ee02a61f1acd** with its original failures and limits intact.
